event: A merchant cart has shed a wheel by the roadside. The driver is cursing loudly but seems fine.
A child sits alone on a milestone, eating an apple and watching the road with unsettling patience.
Two farmers argue heatedly over a fence line that bisects the road. Neither moves to let you pass.
A dead crow has been nailed to a signpost pointing toward Ars Lapis. No one nearby seems to have noticed.
A travelling tinker offers to sharpen blades for a copper each. His hands are steadier than they should be.
The road dips through a shallow ford. The water is murky and cold, but passable.
A pilgrim walking barefoot in the direction of Ars Cultura asks if you've seen any libraries along the road.
An ox has wandered into the road and refuses to move. Its owner is nowhere in sight.
Someone has chalked the Shadowbringers' crescent sigil onto a bridge abutment, then partially scraped it off.
A peddler selling DOL-approved almanacs insists you take one. He keeps checking over his shoulder.
The smell of woodsmoke drifts from a hamlet just off the road. A family watches from their doorway but doesn't wave.
A cart loaded with mined stone from Ars Lapis passes slowly in the opposite direction, the driver's eyes hollow with exhaustion.
A dog trots alongside you for half a mile before stopping abruptly and refusing to go further.
A roadside shrine to an old god has been defaced — the head chiselled off, a DOL sunburst painted over it.
A young courier sprints past at full speed, not stopping to answer any hails.
Rain begins without warning and stops just as suddenly, leaving the road slick and steaming.
A group of monks travelling to Ars Cultura share their fire and bread but ask not to be questioned about their order.
A half-built watchtower sits abandoned at a crossroads. The DOL insignia is carved into the cornerstone.
A wanted notice has been nailed to a tree. The face on it looks uncomfortably like someone the party knows.
A blind beggar sits at the roadside reciting what sounds like encrypted verse. He stops the moment he hears footsteps.
A flock of starlings moves in an unnatural formation overhead — too precise to be natural.
Graffiti on a mile-marker reads: 'THE SUN LIES.' It was written recently — the paint is still tacky.
A horse stands saddled and riderless in the middle of the road, reins dragging in the mud.
Two OOTS soldiers share rations by the road and nod as the party passes — routine, relaxed, watching.
A tree has fallen across the road overnight. It takes time to clear or find a way around.
A woman is burying something small at the roadside. She does not look up.
A travelling bard plays for coins outside a waystation. His songs are all DOL-approved hymns. His eyes are not singing.
The milestone ahead has been moved — deliberately rotated to give a false distance to Ars Pontaris.
A fine layer of grey dust coats everything on the road — mineral runoff from Ars Lapis, blown far by the wind.
A handcart of DOL-confiscated books sits unattended by the road. Several volumes have been thrown into the ditch.
A column of DOL lantern-bearers marches past, each one staring straight ahead. One lingers a beat too long.
A checkpoint has been erected since the last time anyone came this way. The OOTS guards are asking for travel writs.
A wounded man stumbles from the treeline, collapses, and whispers a name before losing consciousness.
A Shadowbringers courier passes in disguise — recognisable only by the crescent-moon pin hidden under their collar. They clock the party and speed up.
The bridge into Ars Pontaris is under OOTS control today. Papers are being checked one by one. The queue stretches back a quarter mile.
A village is being searched. OOTS soldiers move house to house. The villagers stand in the street in silence.
A prisoner transport passes — a wagon with iron bars and four guards. The prisoner inside makes eye contact and says nothing.
A fire has gutted a waystation. Still smouldering. DOL investigators are on the scene and question everyone who approaches.
An OOTS patrol stops the party and demands to search their packs. The senior officer is polite and thorough.
A cart overturned on the road reveals a hidden cargo — not grain as labelled, but printed pamphlets bearing the Shadowbringers' mark.
A lone OOTS agent sits at the roadside eating lunch, watching the party with professional interest. He makes no move.
A dying mule blocks the road. Its panniers are full of sealed correspondence stamped with a DOL wax seal.
A hooded figure steps from the shadow of a toll gate and offers, quietly, to make the party's papers 'look better.' For a price.
The road passes through a narrow canyon. Fresh rockfall has partially blocked it — and fresh boot prints are visible in the rubble.
A Shadowbringers safehouse has been burned and its occupants marched out. The OOTS commander reads from a list of charges loudly, for the road to hear.
A local farmer flags the party down and urgently warns them not to take the northern fork. He won't say why.
A patrol of OOTS cavalry thunders past at speed, heading toward Ars Lapis. No one explains why.
A body has been laid carefully at the roadside, hands folded. It bears no wounds, no insignia, and no identification.
A merchant with a locked strongbox offers to pay the party for an escort to the next town. He's sweating despite the cold.
A section of road has been deliberately torn up — the stones pried out and scattered. Travel through it is slow and loud.
A market day in a village has been shut down by OOTS order. The traders are packing up in angry silence.
A runner from Ars Cultura intercepts the party — breathless, carrying a sealed message meant for someone else entirely.
A second checkpoint appears a mile past the first. Different soldiers, different officer. They've been told to expect someone.
A DOL Inquisitor — gold-trimmed cloak, no weapon visible — stands alone on the road ahead, watching the party approach.
A Shadowbringers sympathiser quietly slips the party a folded note as they pass through a crowded waystation. It reads: 'Don't sleep here.'
Three armed figures step from the treeline with crossbows drawn. They wear no insignia.
A rope snaps taut across the road at horse-chest height. Figures move in the undergrowth on both sides.
A false merchant cart is parked at a bend — the moment the party draws level, the sides drop and armed men pour out.
A Shadowbringers ambush meant for an OOTS convoy has been set on the wrong road. The party walks into it.
An OOTS kill-squad is already in position on the road, hunting a specific target. The party matches the description closely enough.
Wolves — three of them, big and deliberate — pace the treeline and then step onto the road.
A pit trap has been dug across the road and covered with thin boards and dirt. It's deep enough to swallow a horse.
Armed deserters from the DOL conscript corps have taken a waystation by force and are demanding toll from all travellers.
A burned-out escort wagon sits on the road. Two dead guards. Whoever did this left minutes ago — the blood is still wet.
A creature has been driven down from the mountains toward Ars Lapis — massive, confused, and now between the party and the road ahead.
A bounty hunter — working a DOL contract — steps out and names a member of the party by description. She has papers.
A road gang with DOL tacit approval has been taxing travellers in this stretch for weeks. Today they're not in a negotiating mood.
The bridge at Ars Pontaris has been seized by a Shadowbringers cell. DOL reinforcements are twenty minutes out. The bridge is the only crossing.
A pack of grave-ghouls has spilled onto the road from a collapsed mine shaft near Ars Lapis — drawn by light and movement.
A crossbow bolt buries itself in a tree six inches from the party's lead traveller. A voice demands they leave everything on the road and walk.
An OOTS inquisitorial squad — six soldiers, one caster — demands the party submit to a loyalty examination at sword-point.
A desperate Shadowbringers cell, cornered and hunted, mistakes the party for DOL informants and attacks first.
A wyvern circles low over the road, having followed an Ars Lapis ore shipment down from the highland passes.
A DOL execution is underway at a crossroads. The condemned prisoner breaks free during the distraction of the party's arrival.
A mercenary company hired by a rival of the party's patron blocks the road and issues an ultimatum: turn back or be taken.
